title: A Cottage Surrounded by Zombies
notes: Episode 831 (the middle installment) has no subtitle file available locally -- only 0830.txt (Part One) and 0832.txt (Part Two/Three) were read. The reveal, confession, and most physical-clue detail come from 0832.txt; some connective investigative material that likely aired in 831 (e.g. the initial questioning of each crew member, exactly how/when the beard/lipstick/T-shirt mismatches were first raised) is not directly attested and is reconstructed only where 0830/0832 dialogue makes it explicit. Recurring detective-cast nodes (Conan, Kogoro Mouri, Ran, Hattori Heiji, Toyama Kazuha) omitted by convention, as is Inspector Yamamura (Gunma police, pure comic relief with no case-relevant action). The old cases/ file already named the correct culprit (Ria Kawabata) but gave her motive only as 'unspecified (tied to concealing an accidental death from a film shoot eight years earlier)' -- the transcript makes the motive precise and twofold: Harawaki was blackmailing her into starring in his film by threatening to expose her cover-up of Naito Joji's death, and she killed Kyoko because Kyoko was about to realize the staged-suicide video was faked. The old file also collapsed both murders and the 8-year-old backstory death into four generic 'event' nodes and gave the culprit only two thin clue-implication edges; this rebuild decomposes those events into direct typed edges among the real people/objects/locations and expands the evidence to five genuinely comparative clues (envelope-reading trick, video appearance mismatches, misplaced prayer beads, the too-long scream delay, and Ria's steering of the search away from the wardrobe). Naito Joji's death eight years ago is treated as accidental (the search party's own furniture-moving jammed the wardrobe drawer, trapping him) rather than a killing by Ria; her culpability there is concealment/staged rediscovery, not homicide -- only Harawaki's and Kyoko's deaths are murders she commits. case_type: murder.

clues.desc: Toilet paper laid over the sealed envelope blocks the glare that normally hides the writing, letting the subtitle be read from outside without opening it -- explains how the culprit knew the exact wording to fake in Harawaki's 'suicide note.'

In both 'live' videos, Harawaki has no beard and different-colored pants than his corpse, and Kyoko wears no lipstick, has her hair tied back, and wears a lettered 'E' T-shirt matching an old set photo instead of the plain white shirt her body was found in -- proves both videos are old footage replayed and re-recorded, not filmed live.
Prayer beads found in the wardrobe's top drawer could only have fallen there from the bottom drawer, exposing a hidden compartment between them.

Eight years ago, Kyoko was seen standing behind Ria rather than beside her, and Ria's scream came only after an oddly long delay once they entered the room -- implies Ria found Joji's body well before she 'discovered' it and staged the moment for Kyoko.
When Heiji went to search the wardrobe, Ria steered him to check under the bed instead -- behavior only explained if she already knew what the wardrobe concealed.

edges.detail: typed a fake suicide note referencing the subtitle only the sealed envelope contained
